transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time with this, it's probably just normal stress or something, but... well, my wife actually asked me to make the appointment. 

She's been trying really hard to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines again, and I just feel awful because... I don't know, I just don't really feel real happiness or closeness anymore. Even when something at work goes perfectly—and as a manager, I know I should be thrilled when my team does well—I just can't seem to actually feel it. I know I have a good life and I should be happier, so I feel a little embarrassed even complaining about it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... well, I guess it's been a little while now. It, uh... I think it really started after this incident at work. There was a... a retrofit accident. That was about a year and seven months ago. 

I know that probably sounds like a really long time to still be stuck in a rut like this, and I really am trying my best to just move on and be the guy I used to be. I hope it's okay that I'm bringing up something from that far back? I just... I don't want to make a big deal out of it, but I think that's when I stopped feeling like myself. Is that the kind of timeline you were looking for?
Are there any activities that you used to enjoy, but now find pleasure in less often or not at all?

Um, honestly... not really? I mean, I can't really single anything out. I still do all the normal things I've always done, you know? I keep up with all my usual weekend stuff, and I still participate in everything. I really try to stay active and involved so I'm not being a burden on my wife or anyone else. 

So it's not like I've dropped any hobbies or stopped doing things. I guess I just haven't really noticed any specific activity standing out as being less enjoyable... it's just sort of that general flatness I mentioned before, no matter what we're doing. I just keep doing them because I know I'm supposed to, and I want to be a good husband. Does that answer your question okay? I'm sorry if that's not the kind of example you were looking for.
Have you had any periods in the past where you felt extremely down or depressed for a couple of weeks or more?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I've always been a pretty even-keeled guy, you know? I try really hard to just keep a positive attitude and push through things. I don't think I've ever had a time where I was just... down in the dumps for weeks on end, or couldn't get out of bed, or anything like that. 

I really try not to let myself get like that, because I know people depend on me at work and at home. I hope that's the right answer? I just... I don't want you to think I'm someone who just gives up or wallows in things. I've always prided myself on being reliable. Is that helpful?
Do you still feel interested in activities or have you lost interest in things you used to find enjoyable?

Well, um... I think it's pretty much like what I was saying a minute ago. I still have all my same interests, and I make a point to stay involved. I don't want to be one of those guys who just comes home from work and stares at the wall, you know? 

So, I'm still doing all the things I've always done. I really try to stay engaged and be present, especially for my wife. I wouldn't say I've lost interest... I just go through the motions sometimes, but I'm definitely still doing everything. I hope that makes sense? I'm really trying my best to stay on top of things.
Do you feel like you're able to experience pleasure when you're doing things, even if it's not as strong as it used to be?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I really try to appreciate things, I do. But if I'm being completely honest, and I guess this is sort of what brings me in... I don't really feel that true happiness or, you know, closeness anymore. 

Even when my wife goes out of her way to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or if something goes really well at work and everyone else is celebrating... I just kind of feel blank. I still smile and say all the right things, because I don't want to ruin the mood for anyone else. I really want to feel it, I just... can't quite get there. I'm sorry, I know that sounds terrible, like I'm ungrateful or something. I'm really not trying to be. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you felt sad, empty, or depressed most of the day?

Well, um... I think we touched on this a little bit earlier, didn't we? I really haven't had a time like that. I mean, I know I just said I feel a bit blank sometimes, but I wouldn't call it sad or depressed. 

I really try to keep a brave face on, you know? I don't let myself get stuck in a rut for two weeks. I just keep pushing forward and doing what needs to be done. I don't want to be a burden on anyone, so I just... I keep going. I hope I'm not repeating myself too much? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are. I'm really not the type to just sit around feeling sorry for myself, I promise.
Are there things that you used to enjoy that you still do, but no longer find pleasure in?

Well, um... I feel like I might be repeating myself a little bit here, and I'm so sorry if I'm not being clear enough. I think... I mean, I'm still doing all the things I used to enjoy, like I said. The Sunday routines with my wife, staying active with work... I'm still doing all of it. 

I wouldn't say there's anything specific that I've lost pleasure in, because I really do try to find the good in everything. I'm just... maybe not feeling it as strongly right now? But I'm still participating, I'm still there. I really don't want you to think I'm just giving up on the things I love. I'm trying my best to stay positive about it all. Does that answer what you were asking? I hope I'm being helpful.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things that used to bring you pleasure?

Well, um... I guess this is sort of similar to what we were just talking about, right? I really hope I'm not making things confusing for you. 

I wouldn't say I've lost interest. I mean, I still show up for everything. I still go to my son's baseball games, I still help out with the neighborhood watch... I'm still doing all the things I've always done. I really make an effort to stay involved and be there for my family and my community. I don't want to be someone who just checks out, you know? 

So, no, I wouldn't say I've lost interest at all. I'm still very much engaged. I just... I might not be the life of the party right now, but I'm definitely still interested. I hope that makes sense? I'm really trying to give you the right answers here.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Um, no, not really. My weight has been pretty steady, actually. 

I mean, I try to make sure I'm eating right and taking care of myself. I wouldn't want to let my physical health slip or anything like that, you know? So, no big changes up or down, just... just the usual for me. I really try to stay on top of it. 

I hope that's a good thing? I'm really doing my best to keep everything as normal and healthy as possible. Is that the kind of information you need? I want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details.
Do you often feel sad?

Sad? Um... well, no, I wouldn't really use that word. 

I mean, sure, everyone has an off day here and there, right? But I really make a point to keep my chin up. People rely on me at work, and my family needs me, so I don't want to be a burden or bring anyone else down. I really try to just focus on the positives and keep moving forward. 

I'm definitely not sitting around crying or anything like that, I promise. I really try to be strong for everyone around me. I don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in things. Is that... I mean, does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of how I'm handling things.
Do you feel like you're able to experience any pleasure at all, even if it's very mild?

Well, um... I really try to appreciate things, I do. I mean, my wife is wonderful, and she really tries to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, like we used to. And at work, when things go well—and I'm a manager, so I really try to celebrate my team's successes—I smile and I say all the right things. I don't want to bring anyone down.

But... if I'm being completely honest, and I hope it's okay to say this... I guess that's actually kind of what brings me in. I just... I don't really feel that real happiness or closeness anymore. Even when I'm trying my best to enjoy it, it just feels a little blank inside. 

I feel terrible admitting that, because I know I should be grateful for the good things. I don't want to sound unappreciative or like a bad husband. I'm really trying to feel it, I promise. Is it normal to struggle with that? I just hope I'm not doing something wrong by feeling this way.
Do you feel like you're able to enjoy things, even if it's just a little bit?

Um, I... I think I just answered that, right? With the Sunday routines and work? I really hope I explained it okay before. I mean, I *do* try to enjoy things, I really do. I put a lot of effort into participating and being there for my wife and my team. 

I just... like I said, it's just hard to feel that spark right now. But I am trying, I promise. I don't want you to think I've just given up on trying to have a good time or appreciate my life. Did... did you need me to give you more examples? I want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you need to know.
How long have you been feeling this emotional flatness?

Well, um... I guess it's been a while now. I really didn't want to admit it to myself for the longest time, because I kept thinking I could just snap out of it, you know? I didn't want to make a big deal out of nothing.

But, if I really think about it... it started after the retrofit accident at work. That was about... gosh, a year and seven months ago now. I really hope I haven't let it go on too long before getting help. I should have been able to handle it better, I know. Does that timeline make sense to you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
How long have you been feeling this way, exactly?

Oh, um... I think I might have just mentioned that, but I'm happy to say it again if it helps. I want to make sure you have everything you need. 

It's been... well, exactly a year and seven months. Since the retrofit accident. I know I probably should have come in sooner, and I feel bad that I let it drag on this long. I kept hoping I could just fix it myself, you know? I hope it's not too late to try and get back to normal. Is that... is that the exact timeframe you were looking for?
Can you think of anything that brings you even a small amount of joy or pleasure these days?

Um... I know we kind of touched on this, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record or like I'm not trying... but that's actually the main reason I finally made the appointment. 

I just... I don't feel real happiness or closeness anymore. Even when my wife tries so hard to get me to enjoy our old Sunday routines, or when something goes really well at work and I should be thrilled. I go through the motions, and I smile because I want them to be happy, but inside it's just... blank. 

I feel terrible admitting that, especially because my wife is trying so hard. I should be able to feel it, right? I really want to. I hope that doesn't make me sound awful... I'm just trying to be as honest as I can so we can figure this out. Does that answer what you were asking?
Do you feel like your lack of interest in activities is affecting your daily life?

Well, um... I really hate to admit this, because I've always prided myself on being a good manager and a good husband, but... yes, I think it is. I've tried so hard to keep everything running smoothly so no one would worry, but I guess it's slipping. 

At work, I've had to... well, I've started handing off some of the floor responsibilities that I used to manage myself. I just tell my team it's for their professional development, but really, I just can't focus on it. And, um... there was this interview with the regional director recently. I just... I kind of lost my composure and actually walked out. I feel so embarrassed even telling you that, it was incredibly unprofessional of me. I really hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. 

And at home... my wife is so patient, but I know our marriage feels strained right now. I'm there physically, you know, sitting in the living room or at dinner, but I'm just not really participating in our life together. I feel awful about it. I should be doing better for her, and for my team. Is that... is that the kind of information you need to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me fix this.
Do you often feel depressed?

I wouldn't say I feel depressed, exactly. Um... I know that's a strong word, and I don't want to overstate things or make it sound worse than it is. I mean, I don't spend my days crying or feeling completely hopeless like you hear about with real depression. 

It's more just... that blankness I mentioned earlier. Just sort of feeling flat and disconnected. But I'm still getting up every day, still going to work, still trying my best to be present. I don't want you to think I've just completely given up or anything like that. I'm really trying to push through it. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining the difference clearly enough.
Do you feel like you're able to experience any pleasure at all, even if it's very mild, for at least a few days a week?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I wish I could say yes, because I know I should be finding little moments of joy here and there, especially with my wife trying to help me so much. But... no, not even a few days a week. 

It's just that same flat feeling I was talking about. I really hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm not trying to find things to enjoy, because I really am. I want to be able to feel those good things again. I'm sorry, I know that's probably not the answer you were hoping for... is it okay that I'm just being completely honest about that?
Do you feel sad most of the day?

Well, um... no, I wouldn't say I feel sad most of the day. I mean, I don't want to give the impression that I'm just walking around moping all the time. I really do try to keep a positive attitude, especially at work, you know? I want to be a good example for my team. 

Like I said before, it's more of just a... a numbness, I guess. It's not this heavy sadness or anything like that. I'm still functioning, still doing what I need to do. I hope that's helpful... I just want to make sure I'm giving you accurate information so we can figure this out together. Is that the kind of distinction you're looking for?
